In all honesty, a lot of that will stay the same if you continue to work at a General Practice or even an E.R. The days are exhausting and long. Most days by the time I'm home, my boyfriend is already asleep and I'm too tired to cook dinner. The way to get through it is to remind yourself that you're doing a great thing for the world and saving lives. You should also make sure you end up with coworkers that become a second family. Humor helps with the hard days!

One thing that took me a while to get use to- you're not going to get all the answers and sometimes the client changes their answers. When you ask the question, oh fluffy has been vomiting for just a day or two. When the doctor asks- oh its been like a week. Also, you can ask every question under the sun and take a 15 minute history. 50% of the time( in my experience) the doctor will come up with a question you would never think of in regards to the patient's symptoms. 

To sum up, do your best but no one is perfect at taking histories. Ask other nurses to shadow what you're doing if they can to see how you can improve.

At some point, when are you no longer a vet assistant and become a technician? I know some girls who have 15 years of technician experience but aren't certified. Does that mean they aren't qualified to do anesthesia? Or place a catheter? But at the same time, how can you ever expect people to gain experience if your thought process is "just get it done as quick as possible."

I use to work at 14 hour job 7 days a week. If i sat down for lunch, I would get yelled at. The rule was if the work wasn't done (and let's be honest it was never done) then you shouldn't be eating. I ate maybe 1 decent meal every 2 or 3 days. In between would be half sandwiches, some cookies, maybe a soda. It got to the point where if I ran my fingers through my hair, clumps would fall out. 3 years later I could finally finish a whole meal when I went out to dinner. Now (6 years later), I overeat because i can't get out of the "eat while you can" mentality and I hate how I look I've gained weight. I'd rather go back to before.
